newsitem.title: IRAN: Khatami heads for landslide win in Iran election.
newsitem.headline: Khatami heads for landslide win in Iran election.

text.p: Former culture minister Mohammad Khatami headed for a landslide victory on Saturday after first results were announced in Iran's presidential election.

Khatami, considered a moderate among the Shi'ite Moslem clerics who run the Islamic republic, won 6,049,834 of the 8,989,065 votes counted up to 8:00 a.m. (0330 GMT) state radio and television announced.
The state broadcasting media said parliament speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, who had been widely predicted to become Iran's next president, won 2,498,316 votes.
Candidate Mohammad Mohammadi Reyshahri followed with 197,427 and Reza Zevarei was fourth with 177,471.
The turnout was high in Friday's voting, which was twice extended by a total of four hours because of queues of people waiting to cast their ballot.

Some 33 million people aged 15 and over were eligible to vote in the election to replace President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, who must step down in August after completing the maximum two four-year terms allowed by law.
